title: Disbind PDF Into Per-Page PDFs
cap_description: Split a PDF into a sequence of one-page PDFs
documentation:
## Purpose

Splits a PDF into a sequence of one-page PDFs — one item per page. Distinct from [Disbind PDF Into Page Text](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in=media:pdf;op=disbind;out="media:textable;page") in that the output items are *PDF documents*, not extracted text. Use this when downstream caps want to operate on individual pages while keeping the PDF structure intact (e.g. per-page rendering with different parameters, per-page redaction, per-page binding back into a different order).

## Inputs

- A PDF file (path or stdin).
- An optional index range (default: `1-`, every page). Format: `1` (single page), `1-5` (pages 1-5), `3-` (page 3 to end).

## Outputs

A sequence of `media:pdf` items, one valid one-page PDF per emitted page.

## Notes

- Each emitted item is a complete standalone PDF with the page tree, resources, and metadata pdfium produces from the source page; downstream caps that load PDFs work on the items unchanged.
- An index range that matches no pages is a hard error — silently emitting an empty sequence would let downstream pipelines run on nothing without surfacing the empty-range mistake.
- For text-only extraction, use [Disbind PDF Into Page Text](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in=media:pdf;op=disbind;out="media:textable;page").
- For the inverse (concatenating per-page PDFs back into one), use [Bind PDFs](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:bind;in=media:pdf;out=media:pdf).

args.arg_description: Path to the PDF file to process

output.output_description: Per-page PDFs, one item per page
